question: How can all-dielectri photonics crystal enhance fluorescence?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that coupling the pump/excitation light into a PC resonance mode enhances the local electromagnetic field and thus the absorption (excitation rate) of nearby fluorescent species compared with bulk/free-space or unpatterned-substrate absorption.
examples: Coupling the excitation pump into a resonant mode produces an enhanced near-field that increases the absorption of fluorescent molecules on the PC surface.
The PC is designed to support a pump-mode at the laser wavelength, generating a stronger exciting field for surface-attached emitters.
QDs near the PC surface absorb substantially more pump energy than on glass.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that emitted light couples to PC resonant (fluorescent) modes and is radiated/extracted into the far field at a higher rate than emission in free space.
examples: QD emission couples with the PC fluorescent mode and radiates into the far field at a higher extraction rate.
Generated photons are extracted more efficiently from the PC than they would be from an emitter in free space.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that the modified photonic environment of the dielectric PC enhances the spontaneous emission rate and radiative quantum efficiency via the Purcell effect (reduced spontaneous emission lifetime).
examples: The dielectric PC enhances quantum efficiency through the Purcell effect, reducing spontaneous emission lifetime.
Modifying the emitter's photonic environment increases its radiative decay rate and thus quantum efficiency.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that PC resonant modes impose a photonic dispersion that redirects emission into narrow preferred out-coupling angles, improving photon collection efficiency when the detection optics (e.g., objective NA) are matched to those angles.
examples: The PC photonic dispersion dictates a directional angular distribution, so a properly chosen objective NA collects more photons.
Emitted light is redirected into preferred out-coupling directions, enhancing collection efficiency.

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains the underlying mechanism: subwavelength periodicity phase-matches evanescent diffracted orders to spatially localized leaky modes with finite lifetimes, whose resonant energy density scales with the mode Q-factor and is tunable through device parameters.
examples: Higher-order evanescent diffraction is phase-matched to leaky modes that are spatially localized during their finite lifetime.
The energy density at resonance is set by the mode lifetime/Q-factor, controlled by adjusting device parameters.

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that leaky/Fano resonances arise from interference between resonant and direct scattering channels, e.g., backward re-radiated waves constructively interfering with the specular order while forward waves destructively interfere (π out of phase), yielding near-100% reflection at resonance.
examples: Backward re-radiated waves interfere constructively with the zeroth backward-diffracted order while forward waves cancel, giving zero transmission at resonance.
Fano resonances of the PhC arise from interference between the resonance and direct scattering channels, with delocalized wave functions and long lifetimes.

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that the dielectric (absorption-free) nature of the PC enables resonance phenomena such as near-total reflection and strong field enhancement without material loss, distinguishing it from plasmonic (metal-based) enhancement.
examples: In a defect-free, lossless dielectric PC, leaky-mode excitation produces 100% reflection at the resonant wavelength.
Being all-dielectric, the PC avoids metal absorption losses.

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer indicates that the independent mechanisms (excitation, extraction, quantum efficiency, directionality) combine multiplicatively to yield very large total enhancements (e.g., ~3000x for single-QD biosensing), and that the PC environment can also suppress QD blinking, keeping emitters in the 'on' state longer.
examples: The combination of several independent multiplicative effects yields an unprecedented 3000x fluorescence enhancement.
QDs on the PC remain in their on state a larger fraction of the time (blinking suppression), improving photon output.

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer situates the mechanisms in applications such as biosensing with QDs or organic dyes, and acknowledges emitter assumptions: e.g., emitters must lie within the evanescent near field of the PC surface, and near-unity quantum yields may be assumed unchanged.
examples: Enhanced single-QD emission enables digital-resolution biosensing.
Organic dye molecules on a PhC slab show enhanced emission and low-threshold lasing due to Fano resonances.
Because the quantum yield of many dyes is close to unity, it is assumed unchanged by the enhancement effects.
